P16.1 (T5): Finite-energy equations on singular or unibranch varieties
Extend the ﬁnite-energy non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère operator and its existence-and-

P16.7 (T5): Finite-energy equations on nonalgebraizable analytic spaces

10.2    What constitutes a solution
For each axis, state the retained hypotheses and construct the ﬁnite-energy operator together
with the corresponding existence-and-uniqueness theorem. Specify the measure mass and
ﬁnite-energy condition, uniqueness modulo constants and the replacement inputs for com-
pactness, envelopes, energy diﬀerentiation and comparison. An endpoint solving a special
toric measure class does not remove a general axis.

10.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
Problem 10.1. Extend the ﬁnite-energy existence and uniqueness theory for the NA Monge–
Ampère equation beyond the currently proved combinations of smoothness, projectivity,
residue characteristic, valuation, positivity class, support, and algebraizability hypotheses.

    This is not one yes-or-no assertion. Positive characteristic, singular or unibranch varieties,
nondiscrete valuations, big classes, arbitrary support, and nonalgebraizable analytic spaces
require diﬀerent inputs. The known variational proofs use compactness, envelope regularity,
diﬀerentiability of energy, and a comparison principle; deleting a geometric hypothesis is valid
only after replacing every place where it enters. The relevant positive results and their distinct
domains are surveyed in Book Chapter 28, Book Chapter 29.
    The projectivity axis has one logical constraint. A proper algebraic K-scheme endowed
with an ample line bundle is already projective over K [Stacksb, Tag 0B5N]. Thus P16.2
cannot mean that one retains the BFJ line-bundle polarization L while simply deleting the
word “projective.” A nonprojective proper algebraizable extension must ﬁrst replace that
positivity datum—and then construct the corresponding psh, ﬁnite-energy, and comparison
theory—rather than merely rerun the original argument. No canonical replacement with the
required equation theory is asserted here.
    One exact source-stated axis is especially clean. Pille–Schneider observes that the ﬁnite-
energy space can be deﬁned over an arbitrary non-Archimedean ﬁeld, but that the extension of
the Monge–Ampère operator is not known there in general; the discretely valued characteristic-
zero and trivially valued cases are the established endpoints [PS23, Remark 4.4]. This should
be solved before bundling all remaining axes into a single theorem.

Proposition 10.1 (Arbitrary-ﬁeld invariant toric skeletal endpoint). Let K be a complete
nontrivially valued non-Archimedean ﬁeld, XΣ a proper toric K-variety, and L an ample toric
line bundle. If µ is a positive Radon measure on XΣan , is supported on the canonical skeleton
NΣ , gives zero mass to NΣ \NR , and has total mass degL (XΣ ), then there is a toric continuous
singular psh metric on L whose Monge–Ampère measure is µ. It is unique up to multiplication
of the metric by a positive constant.

    Thus nondiscreteness and the arbitrary complete ground ﬁeld cause no obstruction in
this invariant toric, skeleton-supported range. Here “continuous singular” has the source’s
extended-valued meaning: local weights are continuous into R ∪ {−∞}, as in [BGGJK25,
§5.3.1]. It does not imply ﬁnite real-valued weights or ﬁnite energy. This is not an arbitrary-
ﬁeld ﬁnite-energy theorem in the BFJ sense: the result permits a singular potential, requires
torus invariance and skeletal support, and does not construct the general extended Monge–
Ampère operator. In particular, P16.4 and P16.6 retain the respectively nonskeletal and
noninvariant ﬁnite-energy residual scopes.
    There is also a distinct, nonproper algebraic endpoint. Let n > d ≥ 1, let X be a smooth
projective Fano complex variety of dimension n, and let D be a reduced simple-normal-crossing
anticanonical divisor whose dual complex is the standard (d−1)-simplex. For the aﬃne Calabi–
Yau complement X = X \ D, Wang’s Theorem A constructs a continuous non-Archimedean
psh function on X an , over the trivially valued ﬁeld C, whose local Monge–Ampère measure

                                               74

is the canonical Lebesgue measure on the essential skeleton [Wan25]. The source is a version-
one preprint and uses a local CLD/tropical–convex construction. In particular, it neither
constructs the BFJ ﬁnite-energy operator nor treats arbitrary measures or arbitrary aﬃne
varieties. Since X is aﬃne and hence not proper, this endpoint does not answer P16.2; it
only records a special nonprojective algebraic solution after the properness requirement is
also dropped.
    There is a separate ﬁnite-atomic inverse statement which must not be called a ﬁnite-energy
Monge–Ampère theorem. Under its standing assumptions that K is maximally complete and
|K × | = R>0 , Fang ﬁxes an irreducible projective K-variety with an ample line bundle and a
ﬁnite set of graded birational points on its aﬃne cone. For every probability vector on that
ﬁnite set, the source constructs a Shilov-ﬁnite, possibly singular metric having the prescribed
equidistribution measure [Fan25, Proposition 4.8]. The source itself says that comparing this
Banach-algebra measure with the genuine Monge–Ampère measure requires the separate con-
tinuity property of an envelope metric. Thus it supplies neither a continuous semipositive
solution nor the BFJ ﬁnite-energy operator for the prescribed atomic measure, and does not
narrow P16.6.
    There is also a resolved negative regularity chronology. The ﬁrst skeletal-factorization
question of Gubler–Jell–Künnemann–Martin already fails on their toric surface [GJKM19,
Appendix A]. Boucksom–Jonsson then construct a ﬁnite atomic Monge–Ampère measure sup-
ported on a dual complex whose solution is invariant under no retraction attached to any
SNC model; they also construct a divisorial Green function that is not Q-PL [BJ24b, Theo-
rems A and B]. Hence support on a dual complex does not imply factorization through some
reﬁned skeleton. This is a theorem-level obstruction to a proof strategy, not an open regularity
expectation.
    The Rethlas programme treats each axis separately and ﬁrst searches the post-2020 liter-
ature for an existing theorem. Alterations and universal homeomorphisms can address some
algebraic descent questions, but they do not by themselves supply multiplier ideals or dif-
ferentiability in positive characteristic. The unrestricted formulation is open; several strictly
delimited axes are already known.

Throughout Sections 2--8, $k$ is algebraically closed, trivially valued and of characteristic zero. ## 2. Compact algebraic extensions on the original variety

### 2.1. Localization and bounded logarithms

Fix a very ample $H$. If $s$ is a nonzero section, then, without normality,
$$\Gamma(D(s),\mathcal O_X)=\varinjlim_m H^0(X,mH)/s^m. \tag{2.1}$$
On a finite affine trivializing cover this is module localization; the finitely many matching equalizers commute with filtered localization. This proves the assertion for the original structure sheaf. Thus inverting finitely many regular functions $\tau_i/s^{d_i}$ gives the literal chart
$$D(a)=D(s)\cap\bigcap_iD(\tau_i),\qquad a=s\prod_i\tau_i. \tag{2.2}$$
The extra factor $s$ retains the old boundary. Every regular function on this chart is $F/a^m$ for a global section of the appropriate power of $H$.

For a global section $F$, let $\mathfrak b_F$ be the coherent ideal locally generated by its coefficient in a center frame. Its logarithmic norm for the canonical trivial metric is $\log|\mathfrak b_F|$. At each analytic point this is independent of the center frame, since changes of center frame are units in its valuation ring. This also follows from BJ 1.24 and the subsequent definition of section evaluation (S1 LF883--900). Therefore
$$A_{F,N}=\max(\log|\mathfrak b_F|,-N)\in\operatorname{PL}(X) \tag{2.3}$$
for positive rational $N$, by the flag ideal $\mathfrak b_F+(t^N)$ after clearing denominators. If $f=F/a^m$ is a unit on a compact set $W\subset D(a)^{\rm an}$, choose rational clipping levels below the minima of both section logarithms on $W$. Then
$$\log|f|=A_{F,N}-m A_{a,N'}\quad\hbox{on a neighborhood of }W. \tag{2.4}$$
The equality is exact. A uniform approximation to a logarithm is not being substituted.

Analytic units can be treated on smaller compact rational domains as well. In the algebraic reduction of published Ducros 3.2 (S9 LF2087--2127), a rational domain is localized at a nonvanishing denominator $h$, and the functions $b/h^r$ in the original ring are dense in its affinoid algebra. For a unit $f$ choose an approximant $g$ with
$$\|f-g\|_W<\min_W|f|.$$
The ultrametric inequality gives $|g|=|f|$ at **every** point of $W$. A finite list is treated simultaneously. The original domain and principal localization are retained. This uses the precise rational-domain density mechanism in that proof, including its finite rational refinements; density of polynomials on an arbitrary analytic open is not claimed. Norm equality remains true after complete field extension because the same uniform inequality and lower bound pull back.

### 2.2. A finite selected weight has an actual PL extension

Suppose a finite continuous rational-affine selection is supplied near a compact set and its used coordinates are unit logarithms there. Choose compact rational neighborhoods inside its original charts with rational upper/lower bounds; their interiors cover the compact set. They are $\Gamma$-strict with $\Gamma=\exp(\mathbb Q)$, even over the trivial field. Ducros 3.2 applies to these **compact**, $\Gamma$-strict spaces and their **invertible** functions. Their logarithmic images are finite rational polytope complexes of dimension at most $\dim X$. No dimension equality is needed.

Refine the images by the finitely many hyperplanes where the selected affine expressions agree. On a relative open convex cell the distinct expressions have a fixed order. Continuity forces the selected expression class to be locally constant, hence constant on that cell. Continuity supplies its affine value on the closed cell. The result is a rational PL function on a finite compact rational polyhedral complex $T$.

Here is an elementary extension, so no unrestricted tropical selection theorem is hidden. Put $T$ in the interior of a rational box. Cut that box by all rational hyperplanes defining its cells and the expression domains, and barycentrically subdivide the resulting finite rational polytopes. This triangulates the box with $T$ as a subcomplex and each affine piece as a union of simplices. Assign the prescribed rational value to each vertex of $T$, assign zero to the box-boundary vertices, and assign arbitrary rational values to the other vertices. Affine interpolation on every simplex, followed by zero outside the box, gives a continuous finite rational PL function $E$ on the whole Euclidean space, equal to the selection on $T$.

Such $E$ is a difference of finite convex rational PL functions. To verify this directly, take all rational supporting hyperplanes $h_j=0$ of its affine cells. Across any wall, continuity makes the gradient jump normal to the wall. There are finitely many jumps. Choose positive rational $C$ so adding $C\sum_j|h_j|$ makes every oriented normal jump nonnegative. Restriction to each generic line is then convex; continuity handles lines through intersections. Hence $E+C\sum_j|h_j|$ is convex and is the maximum of its finitely many rational affine pieces. The penalty is also a finite convex maximum. Thus $E$ is a finite expression using rational affine combinations, maxima and subtraction.

Replace its unit-log coordinates by the actual global PL functions (2.4). BJ's rational PL space is a vector lattice (S1 LF962--1008), so this expression is a global algebraic PL function agreeing exactly with the local selected weight near the chosen compact set. This construction does not require a positive extension. It also does not identify PL on a polytope with PL on the original bundle without constructing the displayed algebraic functions.

### 2.3. Support-controlled gluing without multiplying PL functions

For compact $K\subset U\subset X^{\rm an}$, choose a continuous bump $b$, equal to one on a neighborhood of $K$, with compact support in $U$. Approximate it by a global rational algebraic PL $p$ with error less than $1/8$, using BJ 2.2 and its lattice proof. Put
$$\chi=\min(1,\max(0,2p-1/2)). \tag{2.5}$$
Then $0\le\chi\le1$, it is one near $K$, and
$$\operatorname{Supp}\chi\subset\{p\ge1/4\}\Subset U.$$ 
Outside $U$, $p<1/8$, and the compact threshold set misses the complement of $U$. This proves controlled support, rather than simply extending a bump by zero.

If finitely many local extensions $E_i$ agree with one continuous function $f$ on opens containing $\operatorname{Supp}\chi_i$, and some $\chi_i=1$ near every point of $K$, choose rational $C$ larger than all necessary compact bounds. Then
$$E=\max_i\bigl(E_i-C(1-\chi_i)\bigr) \tag{2.6}$$
equals $f$ near $K$. Indeed a positive $\chi_i$ puts the point in its agreement chart, where its expression is at most $f$; for $\chi_i=0$ the choice of $C$ suppresses the bounded global $E_i$; a winning $\chi_i=1$ gives equality. Only the tested compact neighborhood is used when $f$ is local. For a global $f$ the same argument applies on all of compact $X^{\rm an}$.

Choose another cutoff $\eta$ equal to one near $K$ with support compact in $U$, and rational $B>\sup_{\operatorname{Supp}\eta}|E|$. The compact signed extension
$$\widetilde f=\max(-B\eta,\min(B\eta,E)) \tag{2.7}$$
equals $f$ near $K$, vanishes on a neighborhood of $X^{\rm an}\setminus U$, and satisfies $|\widetilde f|\le B\eta$. Multiplication of two variable PL functions has **not** been used. A product $\eta E$ need not be PL.

Given a finite open cover, choose compact shrinkings $K_i\subset U_i$ covering $X^{\rm an}$ and cutoffs $\chi_i$ as above. The actual rational PL partition is
$$\rho_1=\chi_1,\qquad \rho_i=\min(\chi_i,1-\sum_{j<i}\rho_j). \tag{2.8}$$
Induction gives $\sum_{j\le i}\rho_j=\min(1,\sum_{j\le i}\chi_j)$. Thus every $\rho_i\ge0$, its support is compact in $U_i$, and $\sum_i\rho_i=1$. No variable denominator occurs.

### 2.4. Exact differences in one actual ample class

For any finite list $a_i\in\operatorname{PL}(X)$, BJ 2.25--2.26 gives $a_i=a_i^+-a_i^-$ with $a_i^\pm=c_i^\pm q_i^\pm$, $c_i^\pm\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}$ and $q_i^\pm\in H(H)$. Choose a common rational $R\ge c_i^\pm$ and set
$$q_{i,R}^\pm=c_i^\pm q_i^\pm+(R-c_i^\pm)0\in H(RH). \tag{2.9}$$
The zero is the actual canonical FS metric on $H$. Tensor products of the generating sections prove the asserted FS membership; denominators are cleared once for the finite list. Thus $a_i=q_{i,R}^+-q_{i,R}^-$ exactly. In original frames $e_\alpha=g_{\alpha\beta}e_\beta$ of $H$, both terms have weights $Rh_{0,\alpha}+q_{i,R}^\pm$ and transition $g_{\alpha\beta}^{NR}$ on the cleared tensor power. Their difference is $a_i$. This is the same algebraic bundle, same cocycle, same reference and same class. Positivity of an abstract numerical class alone is not used.

## 3. Audit and reconstruction of the continuous contact metric bridge

Let a continuous rational contact metric be **already glued** on an ample rational $L$. In a standard very ample frame $e=s_j$ of $qL$, its canonical reference weight is
$$h_{0,j}=q^{-1}\max_l\log|s_l/s_j|,$$
with the $l=j$ term giving a zero floor. Its actual potential is $\phi=b_j-h_{0,j}$, independent of the frame. The finite-floor zero reductions and Section 2 extend its local rational selected weights exactly. Formula (2.6), on the finite compact cover of $X^{\rm an}$, proves
$$\phi\in\operatorname{PL}(X)$$
on the original variety and original $L$.

BJ 2.7/2.31 now supplies an actual algebraic test-configuration line bundle $\mathcal L$ with generic bundle $L$ and model function $\phi$. Take relative integral closure inside that prescribed generic fiber, not absolute normalization. Complete at the test parameter after clearing rational tensor weights over $K=k((t))$, $|t|=e^{-1}$. The model metric is exactly the pullback of the original metric: for a flag ideal its norm is the maximum of the norms of the **separate** ideal generators $a_\lambda t^{-\lambda}$; differences preserve equality. This is an equality at all $K$-analytic points, not only the Gauss section. The model identification uses the original $L$ and its original cocycle.

This is a new resolution of the algebraization dependency in the supplied bridge. GM 2.4 algebraizes a formal blowup ideal, while GM 2.6 cites the separate GK17 8.13 for arbitrary formal line-bundle algebraization (S4 LF249--295). Proper formal-model refinements in the following primary criteria remain background theorems with their precise applications; a title is not presented as their proof.

Over a completed algebraic closure of $K$, pull back a contact support through any smooth analytic curve map into an ordinary weight chart. It becomes
$$h_x=\sum_j a_j\log|f_j|+C,$$

The completed model metric is already rational PL on the original bundle. GR 5.1/5.4, whose full proofs are pinned at S8 LF803--926, therefore give semipositivity on each ordinary point neighborhood. GR's proof lifts the generic reduction point of an entire proper residual curve, retaining the interior condition; its local curve-lifting theorem is pinned at LF489--800. GM 3.11 tests every proper residual curve of the represented global model, using its generic reduction point, a neighborhood and a common dominating model. GM 3.5 and 3.3 then test nefness on the already supplied algebraic model and detect it before field extension. There is no positivity assertion from a Laurent G-cover alone. BE 7.8 now applies over the nontrivial $K$ to the ample $L_K$. It interpolates the nef model with an ample model of the **same** generic bundle. The resulting semiample models give uniform pure FS approximation. The printed $H/A$ switch in its proof is resolved by using one ample model consistently.

# Direct curve Gauss limits for the whole-base trace

This is an unreviewed proof draft, not a solved original problem or an accepted dependency. It combines the actual norm-law draft in round77, Section8, with that round's unreviewed smooth upper-growth and principal-open removal draft, Section7. The independent reviews80/81 are frozen and receive no feedback from this draft.

## 1. Exact domain and binding antecedents

Let \(k\) be algebraically closed, trivially valued and of characteristic zero, with no cardinality restriction. Let \(S=D(a)\subset\mathbb A_k^n\) be a nonempty principal affine open, \(Y\) an irreducible reduced affine \(k\)-variety, and \(\pi:Y\to S\) finite surjective of generic degree \(d\). Let \(u:Y^{an}\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be usc, locally bounded above and finite at the generic trivial point. Retain ONE proper birational witness \(\mu:P\to Y\) on which \(u\circ\mu^{an}\) is locally a decreasing limit of the precise finite rational contact weights of round77. Its continuous supports have the same constant in the supporting inequality and equality.

Assume an actual upper growth bound \(u\le Cg\circ\pi+B\), for an actual AFS exhaustion \(g\) of the original \(S\), and positive \(C\). This upper-bound hypothesis is retained literally. The printed lower-growth convention is not substituted for it.

The following earlier assertions are explicit unreviewed antecedents: (A) round77's smooth affine upper-growth regularization and exact principal-open removal, with its geometric compactification and projective-domination/resolution hypotheses; (B) its generic norm polynomial law over the normal base ring, strictly positive integer residue characters, completed-field compatibility and exact finite AFS trace formulas; (C) the actual ordinary/local contact class and curve restriction mechanism. No preprint envelope theorem, singular EP, general affine theorem over arbitrary valued completed residue fields, or inverse equation is granted.

Conditional on A–C, the claim here is that the actual positive-weight trace
\[
N_\pi u(s)=\sum_{y\in\pi^{-1}(s)}\Gamma_y u(y),\qquad
\Gamma_y\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\quad\sum_y\Gamma_y=d,
\]
is the actual AFS-regularizable extension furnished by A at EVERY base point, including nonflat and removed points. All values on the original variety and the same original witness are retained.

## 2. The extension on the base is constructed first

Shrink to one principal open \(W=D(f)\subset S\) where \(\pi\) is finite étale and \(\mu\) is an isomorphism over the source. Such a nonempty open exists by characteristic zero, generic flatness/separability and the proper closed image of the complement of the witness's isomorphism locus. \(U=\pi^{-1}(W)\) is smooth affine. Apply A to the restriction of that SAME witness and input on \(U\). The finite-map upper bound is an AFS upper bound there: for original source generators, their monic equations over the original base bound their norms by a constant multiple of the base exhaustion; dominated low branches may be appended with explicit positive rational slopes. Retain these original-generator conversions, rather than changing the algebra.

The actual regularizing AFS sequence on \(U\), followed by B's finite-flat polynomial Gauss formula, gives an actual decreasing AFS sequence for \(N_\pi u\) on \(W\). Its limit has the same upper bound \(Cd\,g+B'\), since the positive weights sum to \(d\). Apply A's principal-open removal on the SMOOTH original \(S\) to obtain an actual AFS-regularizable \(v\) on \(S\) with
\[
v=N_\pi u\quad\hbox{on }W^{an}.
\]
No value of \(N_\pi u\) on \(S\setminus W\) is inferred at this stage. It is exactly those values that the next steps identify. Existence and exact geometry in A remain antecedents, not conclusions of this note.

## 3. One actual line through a prescribed analytic point

Fix arbitrary \(s\in S^{an}\), and put \(F=\mathcal H(s)\). The original coordinates give \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\in F^n\), a rational \(F\)-point over \(s\). Choose \(z_0\in W(k)\) outside the finitely many additional closed bad images needed above. Set
\[
c(t)=\alpha+t(z_0-\alpha).
\]
This is an actual affine line over \(F\), restricted to the open parameter locus mapping into \(S_F\); it contains \(t=0\) and \(t=1\). If \(z_0=\alpha\), the prescribed point already belongs to \(W\) and needs no extension argument. Otherwise the line is nonconstant. Because the value at1 is good, the line is generically in \(W_F\). Each inverted defining polynomial has a nonzero restriction to this line. Consequently every positive-radius Gauss point \(\zeta_r\) on the parameter line, sufficiently near0, maps to \(W^{an}\). Its image \(s_r\) tends to \(s\).

The scheme-theoretic inverse image of the line can be nonreduced and nonflat. Reduce it and normalize it, writing \(q:C^\nu\to c(\mathbb A_F^1)\) and \(p:C^\nu\to Y_F\). There are no isolated reduced vertical components: the line is cut by \(n-1\) affine-linear equations in the integral \(n\)-dimensional finite-type \(Y_F\). Krull's height bound and the finite-type dimension formula give dimension at least1 for every minimal component, while finiteness over the line gives dimension at most1. Thus every component is a horizontal curve. The normalization is finite over the line. Each normalized component is a regular curve and hence smooth over the perfect characteristic-zero \(F\); its finite nonconstant map to the regular line is flat. The sum of its generic ranks is \(d\), since over the good open it is the original finite étale base change.

These algebraic inputs have their original hypotheses checked. Primary statements and pertinent proof bodies were read live in [Stacks normalization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXQ), [normal curves and flatness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXX), [normal curve local smoothness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B8Y), [height bound](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BBZ), and [dimension formula](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02JT). The live reads are not pinned whole-page copies or proofs of all recursively cited background results.

## 4. The curve lifts to the ORIGINAL witness

Every component of \(C^\nu\) maps generically into the original witness's isomorphism locus. It therefore has a rational lift to \(P_F\) over \(Y_F\). At a closed curve point its local ring is a DVR. Properness of \(\mu_F\) supplies the unique local extension by the valuative criterion. Finite presentation extends that local map to a neighborhood; separatedness identifies overlapping extensions. This produces the lift of the entire curve to the SAME \(P_F\), and then after any complete extension of \(F\). A new witness for each limit or a dense-open/usc value comparison is not used.

The precise relative extension statement and its full pertinent proof are [Stacks29.43.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BX4). Properness is relative over \(Y_F\); \(P_F\) need not be proper over \(F\).

Now restrict EACH original continuous contact approximant on a neighborhood of the lifted point before taking its decreasing limit. A support \(\sum_j a_j\log|h_j|+b\), with analytic units \(h_j\), pulls back to a harmonic function on the smooth analytic curve. If the pulled continuous weight minus an arbitrary harmonic test has a local maximum, its supporting harmonic function minus that test has the same maximum and is constant locally by the harmonic maximum principle. The weight minus the test is then constant there. Thuillier3.1.12 gives subharmonicity. Decreasing closure3.1.8(ii) gives subharmonicity or the identically-\(-\infty\) alternative on each local connected component. At a point where the limit is finite that alternative is excluded. When the center value is \(-\infty\), usc alone supplies the limit used below.

No current-positivity converse, pullback of an arbitrary current, or AFS regularization theorem over \(F\) occurs. The restriction concerns the actual contact expressions on the original witness.

## 5. Direct radial continuity at the closed centers

If \(F\) has trivial valuation, first adjoin an independent Laurent variable with nontrivial Gauss norm and complete. In either case pass isometrically to a completed algebraic closure \(L\). Its residue characteristic is zero because it contains the trivially valued characteristic-zero \(k\). The finitely many closed points over0 become \(L\)-rational points on the smooth normalized curve. Values pulled from the original \(u\) and \(v\) are unchanged.

The disc coordinate can be obtained directly from a smooth algebraic presentation. At the rational point choose equations \(F_i(z,w)=0\) with the square \(w\)-Jacobian invertible, and translate the point to0. On a sufficiently small polydisc, multiply by the inverse constant Jacobian and make the derivative of the nonlinear remainder in \(w\) have operator norm less than1. For each small \(z\), the map \(w\mapsto w-J^{-1}F(z,w)\) preserves a chosen small closed \(w\)-disc and is a strict contraction. Its iterates converge uniformly, giving analytic \(w(z)\); uniqueness holds also in every complete residue field. Projection to \(z\) and this analytic graph are inverse on the resulting curve neighborhood. Thus the coordinate describes the actual Berkovich disc, not just the completed algebraic local ring. The same contraction argument applies to any analytic \(z'=z+O(z^2)\) after shrinking.

For a rational center \(x\), use a smooth analytic coordinate \(z\) on a sufficiently small disc around it. On a strict closed subdisc \(D_R\), the boundary is the single Gauss point \(\xi_R\). For the pulled limit \(h\), finite at \(x\), the subharmonic comparison definition with a constant harmonic function gives
\[
h(x)\le h(\xi_R).
\]
The boundary value is finite by the strict-domain boundary lemma. Since \(\xi_R\to x\), usc gives the reverse limsup. Hence \(h(\xi_R)\to h(x)\). If \(h(x)=-\infty\), usc gives this directly; locally bounded upper values exclude any \(+\infty\) ambiguity.

This is an actual one-parameter limit on strict discs. Thuillier's pertinent full bodies were read at UTF-8 one-based LF3783–3945, including Definition3.1.5, Proposition3.1.8, Lemma3.1.9 and Corollary3.1.12. The harmonic maximum principle was read at LF3730–3741. The unit harmonic input and its application remain the explicit contact-curve antecedent C. The argument does not use the printed general-\(F\) affine regularization step in Wu6.12.

Apply this both to \(u\circ p\) at every curve center and to \(v\circ c\) at0. The latter is an actual decreasing AFS limit: its finite logarithmic approximants restrict to subharmonic curve functions, and the same comparison and decreasing-limit argument applies.

## 6. Exact Gauss fibers and all weights

At each \(L\)-rational curve center \(x\) over0, the actual finite map has local form
\[
t=b_x z^{e_x}U_x(z),\qquad b_x\ne0,\quad U_x(0)=1.
\]
After shrinking, \(U_x\) has an analytic \(e_x\)-th root: the binomial series converges when \(|U_x-1|<1\), and all integer denominators have norm1 in residue characteristic zero. Replacing \(z\) by \(zU_x^{1/e_x}\) gives the EXACT map \(t=b_x z^{e_x}\), not a leading-order approximation.

For \(r\in|L^\times|\) sufficiently small, its disc map has a unique point over \(\zeta_r\), namely the Gauss point of radius \((r/|b_x|)^{1/e_x}\), with degree \(e_x\). Scale both radii to1. The residue relation is \(Z^{e_x}-T\), irreducible over \(\widetilde L(T)\) by Eisenstein at \(T\); thus the Gauss extension has degree \(e_x\). Properness of the finite curve map ensures all preimages of sufficiently small base discs lie in the union of the finitely many center discs. No branch, center or residue extension is omitted.

For the last neighborhood assertion, fix one small strict closed base disc. Its finite inverse image is compact: finite integral equations bound each algebra generator on the base disc, and the inverse image is the Berkovich spectrum of its finite affinoid algebra. Denominators of the chosen base chart are bounded away from zero after shrinking about0. In that fixed compact inverse image, intersect the preimages of successively smaller closed discs with the closed complement of the union of center neighborhoods. These compact sets decrease to the empty set, because the intersection of the base discs is0 and its entire finite fiber is covered. The finite-intersection property makes one of the sets empty. This proves the whole-fiber neighborhood assertion without discarding points outside the displayed local coordinates.

Before splitting over \(L\), the weights are \(e_x[\kappa(x):F]\). They total \(d\). On the good open their trace is the original finite-flat trace. At0 they coincide with B's canonical norm-law weights, not the possibly larger nonflat fiber dimension: the generic polynomial norm on the finite étale restriction agrees with the product of norms of the normalized horizontal curves. Both coefficient laws are regular at0 and agree generically, hence agree after specialization. The positive residue characters identify their exponents at every original fiber factor. Completed-field compatibility groups the split centers back to each original analytic \(y\). This also proves independence from the chosen good line.

## 7. The actual equality at the formerly omitted point

For the small Gauss radii,
\[
v(s_r)=N_\pi u(s_r)
=\sum_{x\in q^{-1}(0)(L)}e_x\,u\bigl(p(\xi_{x,r})\bigr).
\]
The first equality uses \(s_r\in W^{an}\). The second is the exact finite-flat formula on the normalized line over the good open, with all residue degrees incorporated by the split centers.

Let \(r\downarrow0\) through strict radii in \(|L^\times|\). Section5 identifies each term's limit with \(u(p(x))\), and identifies the left limit with \(v(s)\). The sums are finite and the weights positive. If one center has value \(-\infty\), its term tends to \(-\infty\) while the other finitely many terms remain bounded above locally; otherwise all limits are finite. There is no cancellation of infinities. Section6 groups the center weights into the canonical original \(\Gamma_y\), giving
\[
v(s)=\sum_{y\in\pi^{-1}(s)}\Gamma_yu(y)=N_\pi u(s).
\]
As \(s\) was arbitrary, this identifies the actual extension on the whole base. The argument retains the original witness, the original algebra, the generic degree, every completed residue field, all positive weights and every finite or \(-\infty\) value.

## 8. What is conditional and what remains

This closes the radial-value identification conditional on the exact unreviewed A–C antecedents. It replaces the extra arbitrary-\(\mathcal H(s)\) affine-regularization application by direct contact restriction, strict-disc comparison and exact tame Gauss fibers. Source Wu2609.27610v1 LF2200–2372 was read in full as the printed trace chain to audit, not as independent validation. Its original field/countability and growth hypotheses are not silently extended.

A rigorous new application still needs independent review of A–C and of this whole combined argument, including the analytic contraction and compact finite-affinoid applications above. No claim that their entire primary proof libraries were read is made. After acceptance, the controlled split-piece maximum principle, Runge before strict Hartogs coefficient radii, descending-\(Z\) and singular-stratum inductions, empty-\(Z\) globalization, resolved-nef fiber descent, countable unibranch EP, arbitrary-field finite-data descent, normalization compatibility and the actual singular equation remain to be proved. # Countable-field Runge reconstruction: barriers, uniform pole clearing and split traces

This is a new unreviewed proof draft. It does not close original P16.1. The exact round77 partial proof now has an actual independent round80 PASS, with every conditional geometric antecedent retained. Its complete body and report, rather than an assertion that singular EP is known, are the available background. The direct whole-base curve/Gauss trace in continuation86 remains new mathematics that must be reconstructed independently.

## 1. Domain and dependency ledger

Let \(k\) be a **countable**, algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field. Let \(Y=\operatorname{Spec}R\) be reduced irreducible affine. Keep its original ring and generators. A weak input \(u\), finite at the generic trivial seminorm, is given on ONE proper birational witness by local decreasing finite contact weights and has an actual upper bound \(u\le Cg+B\), for an original affine FS exhaustion \(g\ge0\).

Three applications still require complete verification: (T) the continuation86 whole-base positive-weight weak trace, including all original and exceptional values; (G) controlled affine FS approximation in the prescribed original reference on a possibly singular affine variety, starting with an already genuine affine FS limit; and (H) the Runge Hartogs criterion in that same reference. The compact rational PL representation and continuous nef/FS bridge needed for G are in the accepted round77/80 scope. Neither singular EP nor an onto map from a resolution is an antecedent.

Below, the pole-clearing estimate is an independent algebraic repair. The split-fiber contradiction is conditional on T and G. The explicit strict barrier removes reliance on an unread strictly-convex extension proposition. H and the singular-stratum projection/local-to-global applications remain tasks for the next native reconstruction.

## 2. A failure in the printed denominator argument

In the diagnostic primary text, Wu 2609.27610v1, LF1846–1872, the implication \(p\notin(f)\Rightarrow p\) nonzero somewhere on \(V(f)\) is false for nonradical principal ideals. Already take \(R=k[x]\), \(f=x^2\), \(p=x\). A branch \(\tfrac32\log|p/f|\) has pole growth at most \(\log|f^{-1}|\), although its displayed denominator exponent times slope is \(3/2>1\). Thus the claimed inequality \(q r\le c\) cannot be used.

This is a defect in that proof step, not a counterexample to the desired hull estimate. The repair retains normalization as an algebraic auxiliary only and evaluates every final inequality on the original variety.

## 3. The uniform annihilator repair

Let \(f\ne0\) in \(R\), \(b\in R_f\setminus\{0\}\), and \(q,c\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\). Suppose
\[
q\log|b|\le\max(G,c\log|f^{-1}|)+B\quad\text{on }Y_f^{an},
\]
where \(G\) is a finite continuous original affine FS function. Choose \(N\ge1\) with \(m=Nc/q\in\mathbb Z\), and put \(h=b^Nf^m\in R_f\).

The finite normalization \(\bar R\) is a Noetherian normal domain. For any height-one prime of \(\bar R\) containing \(f\), let \(\operatorname{ord}_E\) be its DVR valuation. Its original affine functions have nonnegative order, so \(G\) is bounded along \(e^{-t\operatorname{ord}_E}\), \(t\to+\infty\). The growth inequality gives \(q\operatorname{ord}_E(b)+c\operatorname{ord}_E(f)\ge0\), hence \(\operatorname{ord}_E(h)\ge0\). At height-one primes not containing \(f\), \(h\in R_f\) already has nonnegative order. The intersection-of-height-one-localizations criterion gives \(h\in\bar R\), so \(h\) is integral over \(R\).

The finite algebra \(R[h]\) is contained in \(R_f\). A finite \(R\)-module generating list therefore has denominators killed by one power \(f^M\). Consequently
\[
f^M h^j\in R\quad\text{for EVERY }j\ge0
\]
with one \(M\), independent of \(j\). No claim that a power of every integral element belongs to \(R\) is made.

Let \(L\subset Y_f^{an}\) be compact and \(x\in\widehat L_Y\cap Y_f^{an}\). Every original polynomial \(f^Mh^j\) satisfies its hull bound. Taking \(j\)-th roots and letting \(j\to\infty\) gives
\[
|h(x)|\le\sup_L|h|.
\]
If the right side is zero, the same assertion follows directly from any positive \(j\). Since \(|\log|f||\le M_1\) on \(L\cup\{x\}\), it follows that
\[
q\log|b(x)|\le\sup_L q\log|b|+2cM_1.
\]
Additive branch constants are harmless. Applied to each branch of an actual affine FS maximum with the displayed upper bound, this proves the approximate local hull inequality without the false denominator-order assertion.

The primary algebraic inputs are finite normalization (Stacks 33.27.1, tag 0BXQ), the height-one intersection criterion (10.157.6, tag 031T), and the DVR criterion (10.119.7, tag 00PD). The finite-module denominator argument is given in full above. G is still needed to pass this estimate from controlled FS approximants to an already genuine local input.

## 4. Explicit soft maxima on extended tropical space

For \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_s)\in(\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\})^s\), choose rational \(\beta\ge\log(s+1)\), and define
\[
\chi(t)=\beta^{-1}\log\left(1+\sum_{\ell=1}^s e^{-\beta t_\ell}\right).
\]
Use \(e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0\). Then \(0\le\chi-\max(0,-t_1,\ldots,-t_s)\le1\). At a point \(t\), use derivative \(c_\ell=-e^{-\beta t_\ell}/(1+\sum e^{-\beta t_j})\) for finite coordinates and \(c_\ell=0\) for infinite coordinates. The affine support \(\ell(t')=\sum c_jt'_j+C\), with zero coefficients omitted, has equality at \(t\), lies below \(\chi\), and has a strict gap away from every neighborhood of \(t\).

For the last assertion, on the finite coordinates the log-sum-exp Bregman difference is strictly positive away from \(t\) and tends to infinity at infinity: the constant exponential has strictly positive weight, so the sum of the other support weights is strictly less than one. On coordinates infinite at \(t\), the omitted exponentials increase \(\chi\) strictly whenever such a coordinate is finite. Once the finite coordinates lie in a compact neighborhood of their target, imposing \(t'_j\le A\) on any omitted coordinate gives a uniform positive increase. These two facts prove the uniform gap on the complement of a product neighborhood, and hence on the complement of any larger prescribed neighborhood.

For rational \(\beta\), the tropical pullback of \(\chi\) admits global uniform rational convex-PL approximants from above. Use its convex conjugate, the continuous convex entropy function \(e(p)=\beta^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^s p_i\log p_i\) on the compact probability simplex. Take a rational grid triangulating every coordinate face with mesh tending to zero, and rational vertex heights lying slightly above \(e\). Their convex roof is at least \(e\) by convexity, and is at most the barycentric interpolation on each small simplex; uniform continuity bounds its excess by a rational \(\delta\downarrow0\). Subtract \(\delta\) and take conjugates. Each conjugate is the maximum of the affine functions associated to lower-hull grid vertices, with rational nonnegative slopes and rational heights, and lies between \(\chi\) and \(\chi+\delta\) globally. The same argument on every coordinate face includes infinite tropical coordinates. The summable constant-shift construction below gives decreasing approximants; no minimum of convex primal functions is used.

Pullback affine branches are positive rational combinations of original \(\log|f_j|\). Clearing the common slope denominator makes them logarithms of original monomials. A low constant branch and sufficiently small positive branches of all original generators can be retained. Thus this is an actual affine FS approximation, not an abstract convex completion.

## 5. A countable strict barrier and its local modification

Enumerate all \(f_i\in R\), retain generators \(z_1,\ldots,z_a\), and pull back the preceding \(\chi\) by their logarithmic norms. Write the resulting nonnegative functions as \(\rho_j\). Let \(g=\max(0,\log|z_1|,\ldots,\log|z_a|)\). Polynomial degree bounds over the trivially valued field give rational \(\gamma_j>0\) such that
\[
0\le\gamma_j\rho_j\le2^{-j}(g+1).
\]
Then \(\rho=\sum_j\gamma_j\rho_j\) converges locally uniformly, is finite continuous, and satisfies \(0\le\rho\le g+1\). The upper partial sums
\[
\rho^{(r)}=\sum_{j\le r}\gamma_j\rho_j+2^{-r}(g+1)
\]
decrease to \(\rho\). Each has global uniform affine FS approximation. If \(v_r\) approximates \(\rho^{(r)}\) with error \(\epsilon_r\), choose rational shifts \(B_r\downarrow0\) with \(B_r-B_{r+1}\ge\epsilon_r+\epsilon_{r+1}\). Then \(v_r+B_r\) decreases. This proves actual FS regularizability directly.

Given \(x\) and an open neighborhood \(U\), choose finitely many original functions whose tropical inverse image of a product neighborhood is contained in \(U\). Choose a sufficiently large index \(j\) and replace \(\rho_j\) by its affine support \(\ell_j\) at \(x\). Then
\[
\rho'=\rho-\gamma_j\rho_j+\gamma_j\ell_j,\qquad
\rho'\le\rho,\quad\rho'(x)=\rho(x),\quad\rho'\le\rho-\delta\ \text{outside }U
\]
for some \(\delta>0\). The displayed subtraction specifies the replacement; positivity is proved from the expression as the sum of the OTHER \(\rho_i\) and a positive combination of unit logarithms near \(x\), not by subtracting arbitrary psh functions.

To regularize a real positive coefficient \(a\log|f|\), choose nested rational intervals \(a_r\uparrow a\), \(b_r\downarrow a\), \(a_r>0\), and use \(\max(a_r\log|f|,b_r\log|f|)\). These decrease at positive, negative and zero logarithmic norms, including \(-\infty\). Sum them, approximate the additive constant from above, and append \(\epsilon_rg-r\) with positive rational \(\epsilon_r\downarrow0\). The last branch retains every original generator and tends to \(-\infty\) at every original point. Apply the same finite-sum/tail and summable-error construction to the other \(\rho_i\). This gives actual decreasing original affine FS approximants for \(\rho'\), including its \(-\infty\) locus.

This construction genuinely uses countability. It does not claim a single such barrier over an arbitrary-cardinality field.

## 6. The maximum principle away from the bad set

Assume \(u\) itself is already genuinely affine-regularizable on an affine cover of \(Y\setminus Z\). This stronger, intended assumption replaces the printed assertion that only \(u+c\rho\) is locally regularizable; the latter does not justify subtracting \(c\rho\).

Set \(u_c=u+c\rho\), \(c>0\). If \(x\in\widehat L_Y\setminus Z^{an}\) violates \(u_c(x)\le\sup_Lu_c\), choose a small \(\epsilon>0\) and the genuine function \(a=\max_i\log|f_i|\), where the \(f_i\) generate the ideal of \(Z\), so that the violation survives for \(u_c+\epsilon a\). Its maximum on the compact hull is attained at a point \(y\notin Z^{an}\cup L\). Choose a relatively compact open neighborhood \(V\) of \(y\), with closure in one principal good affine chart and disjoint from \(L\). Let \(K=\partial V\cap\widehat L_Y\).

Replace \(\rho\) by the local modification \(\rho'\) at \(y\). The weak function \(w=u+c\rho'+\epsilon a\) has \(w(y)\ge\sup_Kw+c\delta\). On the chosen good chart it is already a genuine affine FS limit and has a global original-ring FS upper bound. Rossi's local hull principle gives \(y\in\widehat K_Y\). G followed by the uniform-annihilator estimate gives \(w(y)\le\sup_Kw\), a contradiction.

For Rossi's principle itself, the standard argument is valid once the continuous compact PL bridge is used: if an original polynomial exceeds its boundary hull bound, glue \(\max(Cg_0,\log|p|-t)\) on \(V\) to \(Cg_0\) outside, where \(g_0\ge0\) vanishes on a thick polynomial polytope containing \(\widehat L_Y\). On a whole boundary collar the first branch wins. The result is continuous rational PL with harmonic supports and the same original reference. The accepted algebraic-first nef/FS bridge supplies a uniform global FS approximation. It separates \(y\) from \(L\), contradicting its hull membership. No singular envelope is invoked.

## 7. Corrected split-fiber trace contradiction

Suppose \(\pi:Y\to S\subset\mathbb A_k^n\) is finite, \(S\) affine open, \(\pi|_Z\) is a closed immersion onto its image, and \(Z\) and \(\pi^{-1}(\pi Z)\setminus Z\) are disjoint closed subsets. If \(\{u_c<0\}\) is not Runge, choose compact \(L\) and normalize \(\sup_{\widehat L_Y}u_c=0>\sup_Lu_c=-\delta\). A maximizing \(x\) belongs to \(Z^{an}\) by the preceding principle.

The hull \(C=\widehat{\{\pi(x)\}}_S\) lies in \((\pi Z)^{an}\). Its finite preimage splits into two disjoint compact pieces, one in \(Z\), the other in the complementary closed subset. Disjoint neighborhoods \(A_1,A_2\) can be chosen, and properness gives a base neighborhood \(A\) of \(C\) whose whole preimage lies in \(A_1\cup A_2\).

Choose an original nonnegative affine FS \(g_S\) and a strict polynomial presentation \(U\) containing \(C\), such that \(g_S=0\) on \(U\), \(\{g_S\le1\}\) is compact in \(A\), and \(W=\{g_S<1\}\). This uses finite polynomial separation and thickened rational inequalities. It does not identify topological interiors with strict inequalities for arbitrary degenerate presentations. The sets \(W_i=\pi^{-1}(W)\cap A_i\) are disjoint OPEN sets with controlled compact closures; the printed claim that these interiors are compact is discarded.

Extend their indicator \(h=1\) on \(W_1\), \(0\) on \(W_2\) by
\[
H=\max(3g_S\circ\pi-1,h)\ \text{on }\pi^{-1}(W),\qquad
H=3g_S\circ\pi-1\ \text{outside}.
\]
The reference wins on a whole collar. The trace of this finite continuous input is continuous by the accepted canonical norm formula. On \(U\) it equals the positive integer
\[
\Gamma_1(s)=\sum_{y\in\pi^{-1}(s)\cap W_1}\Gamma_y.
\]
It is LOCALLY constant. Shrink to one neighborhood of \(\pi(x)\) on which it equals \(\gamma\); no connectedness of all of \(U\) is assumed.

If \(\gamma>1\), usc and properness give a further base neighborhood whose whole \(W_1\)-fiber lies in \(\{u_c<\delta/[2(\gamma-1)]\}\). At the central fiber its \(W_1\)-part is just \(x\), because \(\pi|_Z\) is a closed immersion and the other closed piece avoids \(A_1\). If \(\gamma=1\), omit the divided bound: positivity and integer weights imply that every \(W_1\)-fiber has exactly one point of weight one.

Choose a relatively compact open \(V\) around \(x\) whose closure lies in the controlled source neighborhood. Put \(K=\partial V\cap\widehat L_Y\), and use \(\rho'\) with gap \(\delta'>0\) there. Then \(u'_c=u+c\rho'\) equals zero at \(x\), lies below \(u_c\), and satisfies \(u'_c\le-c\delta'\) on \(K\). The factor \(c\) is retained.

Set \(v=u'_c\) on \(W_1\), \(v=0\) on \(W_2\). It is weak on the restriction of the SAME witness. Let \(M\ge0\) bound it above on the controlled compact preimage, and choose \(C>M+1+\delta\). Extend
\[
\widetilde v=\max(Cg_S\circ\pi-\delta,v)\ \text{on }\pi^{-1}(W),\qquad
\widetilde v=Cg_S\circ\pi-\delta\ \text{outside}.
\]
On \(U_1\) it is \(\max(u'_c,-\delta)\), and on \(U_2\) it is zero. The reference wins on an entire outer collar, and the original witness still gives its weak upper-growth property. T gives an ACTUAL regularizable \(w=N_\pi\widetilde v\) on \(S\), and \(w\circ\pi\) is genuinely regularizable on \(Y\). Finite integral generator bounds and the prescribed outside affine FS branch retain every original source generator in this pullback.

Rossi gives \(x\in\widehat K_Y\), hence \(w(\pi x)\le\sup_Kw\circ\pi\). At \(x\) the left side is zero. At \(z\in K\cap Z^{an}\), the only \(U_1\)-branch over \(\pi z\) is \(z\), with total weight \(\gamma\), so
\[
w(\pi z)\le-\gamma\min(\delta,c\delta')<0.
\]
At \(y\in K\setminus Z^{an}\), the off-bad-set maximum principle gives \(\widetilde v(y)=-\delta\). If \(\gamma>1\), all other \(U_1\)-branches are bounded by \(\delta/[2(\gamma-1)]\), and their total weight is at most \(\gamma-1\); thus \(w(\pi y)\le-\delta/2\). If \(\gamma=1\), there are no other \(U_1\)-branches and \(w(\pi y)=-\delta\). The \(U_2\)-branches contribute zero. This contradicts the hull inequality and proves the split-case Runge conclusion conditional on T and G.

## 8. Remaining applications

The descending bad-set chain is \(Z_{r+1}=Z_r\cap\overline{\pi^{-1}(\pi Z_r)\setminus Z_r}\). Its dimension drop, localization outside \(\pi^{-1}(\pi Z_{r+1})\), application to the Hartogs function \(\log|w|+u\) on \(Y\times\mathbb A^1\), and final local-to-global conclusion must all be proved with one product witness and the original FS generators. The Hartogs Gauss coefficient radius formula is applied only AFTER genuine Runge exhaustions exist; radius \(+\infty\) corresponds to \(u=-\infty\). The smooth-stratum finite projection must also be constructed with the correct inverse image of the base affine open.

Even after these countable-field affine gates, resolved-nef fiber constancy, actual singular global descent, finite-data descent to arbitrary-cardinality fields, normalization/E1/product compatibility, and the full raw-mass finite-energy equation remain to be checked. This draft makes no assertion that those antecedents follow from the two new partial PASS reports.

      "literal": "Notation and conventions.\n     • We use the standard abbreviations usc for ‘upper semicontinuous’, lsc for ‘lower\n       semicontinuous’, wlog for ‘without loss of generality”, and iff for ‘if and only if’.\n       We also use PL for ‘piecewise linear’, snc for ‘simple normal crossing’, and psh for\n       ‘plurisubharmonic’.\n     • Following the Bourbaki convention, all compact and locally compact topological\n       spaces are required to be Hausdorff.\n     • A net in a set X is a family (xi )i∈I of elements of X indexed by a directed set, i.e.\n       a partially preordered set in which any two elements are dominated by a third one.\n       A subnet of (xi )i∈I is a net of the form (xϕ(j) )j∈J where ϕ : J → I is increasing and\n       final, i.e. for each i ∈ I there exists j ∈ J with ϕ(j) ≥ i. A (Hausdorff) topological\n       space X is compact iff every net in X admits a convergent subnet.\n     • If X is a Hausdorff topological space, and ϕ : X → R ∪ {±∞} is any function, then\n       the usc regularization ϕ? of ϕ is the smallest usc function with ϕ? ≥ ϕ. Concretely,\n       ϕ? (x) = lim supy→x ϕ(y). The lsc regularization is defined by ϕ? = −(−ϕ)? .\n     • We work over an algebraically closed field k, for the most part of arbitrary charac-\n       teristic. In this paper, a variety (over k) is a separated k-scheme of finite type that\n       is reduced, but not necessarily irreducible, nor even equidimensional.\n\f10                      SÉBASTIEN BOUCKSOM AND MATTIAS JONSSON\n\n     • For any variety X, we denote by Pic(X) the Picard group of isomorphism classes of\n       line bundles. Elements of the associated Q-vector space Pic(X)Q := Pic(X) ⊗Z Q\n       can be viewed as isomorphism classes of Q-line bundles.\n     • If X is a projective variety, we denote by N1 (X) the finite dimensional R-vector\n       space of numerical classes of R-Cartier divisors on X. It comes with a surjective\n       linear map Pic(X)R → N1 (X) induced by L 7→ c1 (L) .\n     • Ample classes form a nonempty open convex cone Amp(X) ⊂ N1 (X), whose closure\n       is the closed convex cone Nef(X) ⊂ N1 (X) of nef classes. For θ, θ0 ∈ N1 (X), we\n       write θ ≥ θ0 if θ − θ0 is nef. We generally denote by θ an element of N1 (X), and by\n       ω an element of Amp(X).\n     • The cone Psef(X) ⊂ N1 (X) of pseudoeffective classes is defined as the closed convex\n       cone generated by classes of effective R-Cartier divisors; its interior Big(X) is the\n       cone of big classes.\n     • A section of a line bundle on X is regular if it does not vanish identically along any\n       irreducible component of X.       "literal": "Definition 1.10. We say that a test configuration X for X is integrally closed if the scheme\nX is integrally closed in the generic fiber Xk($) of π : X → A1 .\n  In other words, X is integrally closed iff it can be covered by affine open subsets U =\nSpec A such that the k[$]-algebra A is integrally closed in Ak($) . Note that X is normal iff\nX is normal and X is integrally closed.\nExample 1.11. The trivial test configuration Xtriv = X × A1 is integrally closed.\n   The integral closure of any test configuration X in Xk($) defines a finite, Gm -equivariant\nmorphism Xe → X (because the scheme X , being of finite type over a field, is excellent),\nwhich induces an isomorphism on the generic fibers over A1 .
